chapter: World's Greatest Jazz Band and Denver
title: How he came to the World's Greatest Jazz Band; Ed Hall
summary: Dance asks how Gus joined the band, he recalls the Black clarinettist, Ed Hall.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Well, listen, I'll tell you what stage we've got to, when you appeared with the World's Greatest Jazz Band, which was -- of course, Dick Gibson was back of that, wasn't he?
Oh, yes, yes.
Well, how did that happen? I mean, who approached you on that? Bob Zirk or [Zoot] or --
No, it was a bass player, Jack Lesberg.
Oh.
I came down to the Half Note one night and Lesberg came in.
You integrated that band, didn't you?
Yes, I did.
I thought so. So he came in.
No, no, I didn't. They had a clarinet player before -- what's his name? He died.
A black clarinet player?
Yes.
Who did he work with before?
Oh, he worked with a lot of jazz groups in New York. Very good clarinet player. I'll have to figure out -- let's see, what is his name?
Funny. Was he with bands? Big bands?
He could have been. I'm quite sure
he was.
I can't place him. Oh, you don't -- I know who you mean. It's Ed Hall.
Ed Hall, that's right. That's who I'm mean -- Ed Hall.
(End of Side One.)
